249	        eprintln!("  5. Get both chids, jj describe both with correct ochids");
250	        eprintln!("  6. Remove jj from both (git clean -xdf)");
251	        eprintln!("  7. gh repo create {session_repo} {visibility}, push");
252	        eprintln!("  8. git submodule add .claude, second commit in code repo");
253	        eprintln!("  9. gh repo create {code_repo} {visibility}, push");
254	        eprintln!("  10. jj git init --colocate on both repos");
255	        eprintln!("  11. Create Claude Code symlink");
256	        return Ok(());
257	    }
258	
259	    let v = args.verbose;
260	
261	    // Step 1: Create directories
262	    eprintln!("Step 1: Creating project directories...");
263	    std::fs::create_dir_all(&session_dir)?;
264	
265	    // Step 2: git init + jj init on both repos
266	    eprintln!("Step 2: Initializing repos...");
267	    run("git", &["init"], &project_dir, v)?;
268	    run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &project_dir, v)?;
269	    run("git", &["init"], &session_dir, v)?;
270	    run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &session_dir, v)?;
271	
272	    // Step 3: Write config files
273	    eprintln!("Step 3: Writing config files...");
274	    std::fs::write(project_dir.join(".vc-config.toml"), VC_CONFIG_CODE)?;
275	    std::fs::write(project_dir.join(".gitignore"), GITIGNORE_CODE)?;
276	    std::fs::write(session_dir.join(".vc-config.toml"), VC_CONFIG_SESSION)?;
277	    std::fs::write(session_dir.join(".gitignore"), GITIGNORE_SESSION)?;
278	
279	    // Step 4: jj commit both with placeholder ochids
280	    eprintln!("Step 4: Committing both repos with placeholder ochids...");
281	    run(
282	        "jj",
283	        &["commit", "-m", "Initial commit\n\nochid: /none"],
284	        &project_dir,
285	        v,
286	    )?;
287	    run(
288	        "jj",
289	        &["commit", "-m", "Initial commit\n\nochid: /none"],
290	        &session_dir,
291	        v,
292	    )?;
293	
294	    // Step 5: Get both chids, then describe both with correct ochids
295	    eprintln!("Step 5: Setting ochid cross-references...");
296	    let code_chid = jj_chid("@-", &project_dir)?;
297	    let session_chid = jj_chid("@-", &session_dir)?;
298	
299	    let code_desc = format!("Initial commit\n\nochid: /.claude/{session_chid}");
300	    let session_desc = format!("Initial commit\n\nochid: /{code_chid}");
301	    run("jj", &["describe", "@-", "-m", &code_desc], &project_dir, v)?;
302	    run(
303	        "jj",
304	        &["describe", "@-", "-m", &session_desc],
305	        &session_dir,
306	        v,
307	    )?;
308	
309	    if v {
310	        let hash = run("git", &["rev-parse", "HEAD"], &project_dir, v)?;
311	        eprintln!("  code repo: chid={code_chid} hash={hash}");
312	        let hash = run("git", &["rev-parse", "HEAD"], &session_dir, v)?;
313	        eprintln!("  .claude:   chid={session_chid} hash={hash}");
314	    }
315	
316	    // Step 6: Set bookmarks (creates git branches), then remove jj
317	    // Bookmarks must be set before removing .jj/ so git has a 'main' branch to push
318	    eprintln!("Step 6: Setting bookmarks and removing jj...");
319	    run(
320	        "jj",
321	        &["bookmark", "set", "main", "-r", "@-"],
322	        &project_dir,
323	        v,
324	    )?;
325	    run(
326	        "jj",
327	        &["bookmark", "set", "main", "-r", "@-"],
328	        &session_dir,
329	        v,
330	    )?;
331	    // Clean .claude first, then code repo with --exclude to preserve .claude/
332	    run("git", &["clean", "-xdf"], &session_dir, v)?;
333	    run(
334	        "git",
335	        &["clean", "-xdf", "--exclude", ".claude"],
336	        &project_dir,
337	        v,
338	    )?;
339	    // After removing .jj/, git HEAD is detached — reattach to main
340	    run("git", &["checkout", "main"], &session_dir, v)?;
341	    run("git", &["checkout", "main"], &project_dir, v)?;
342	
343	    // Step 7: Create .claude GitHub repo and push
344	    let session_url = format!("git@github.com:{session_repo}.git");
345	    eprintln!("Step 7: Creating GitHub repo {session_repo}...");
346	    run(
347	        "gh",
348	        &["repo", "create", &session_repo, visibility],
349	        &project_dir,
350	        v,
351	    )?;
352	    run(
353	        "git",
354	        &["remote", "add", "origin", &session_url],
355	        &session_dir,
356	        v,
357	    )?;
358	    run_retry(
359	        "git",
360	        &["push", "-u", "origin", "main"],
361	        &session_dir,
362	        args.push_retries,
363	        args.push_retry_delay,
364	        v,
365	    )?;
366	
367	    // Step 8: Add .claude as submodule — second commit in code repo
368	    eprintln!("Step 8: Adding .claude as submodule...");
369	    // Remove .claude directory so git submodule add can re-clone it
370	    std::fs::remove_dir_all(&session_dir)?;
371	    run(
372	        "git",
373	        &["submodule", "add", "--force", &session_url, ".claude"],
374	        &project_dir,
375	        v,
376	    )?;
377	    let submodule_body = format!("Add .claude submodule\n\nochid: /.claude/{session_chid}");
378	    run("git", &["add", "."], &project_dir, v)?;
379	    run("git", &["commit", "-m", &submodule_body], &project_dir, v)?;
380	
381	    // Step 9: Create code GitHub repo and push
382	    let code_url = format!("git@github.com:{code_repo}.git");
383	    eprintln!("Step 9: Creating GitHub repo {code_repo}...");
384	    run(
385	        "gh",
386	        &["repo", "create", &code_repo, visibility],
387	        &project_dir,
388	        v,
389	    )?;
390	    run(
391	        "git",
392	        &["remote", "add", "origin", &code_url],
393	        &project_dir,
394	        v,
395	    )?;
396	    run_retry(
397	        "git",
398	        &["push", "-u", "origin", "main"],
399	        &project_dir,
400	        args.push_retries,
401	        args.push_retry_delay,
402	        v,
403	    )?;
404	
405	    // Step 10: Re-initialize jj on both repos
406	    eprintln!("Step 10: Re-initializing jj on both repos...");
407	    run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &project_dir, v)?;
408	    run(
409	        "jj",
410	        &["bookmark", "set", "main", "-r", "@-"],
411	        &project_dir,
412	        v,
413	    )?;
414	    run("jj", &["bookmark", "track", "main@origin"], &project_dir, v)?;
415	    let code_chid_final = jj_chid("@-", &project_dir)?;
416	
417	    run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &session_dir, v)?;
418	    run(
419	        "jj",
420	        &["bookmark", "set", "main", "-r", "@-"],
421	        &session_dir,
422	        v,
423	    )?;
424	    run("jj", &["bookmark", "track", "main@origin"], &session_dir, v)?;
425	    let session_chid_final = jj_chid("@-", &session_dir)?;
426	
427	    // Step 11: Create Claude Code symlink
428	    eprintln!("Step 11: Creating Claude Code symlink...");
429	    let symlink_dir = {
430	        let home =
431	            std::env::var("HOME").map_err(|_| "HOME environment variable not set".to_string())?;
432	        PathBuf::from(home).join(".claude").join("projects")
433	    };
434	
435	    let meta = symlink::probe_symlink(
436	        &symlink_dir.join(symlink::encode_path(
437	            project_dir
438	                .to_str()
439	                .ok_or("project path is not valid UTF-8")?,
440	        )),
441	    );
442	    let plan = symlink::compute_plan(&project_dir, Path::new(".claude"), &symlink_dir, meta)?;
443	    symlink::execute_plan(&plan, false)?;
444	
445	    eprintln!("Done! Project created at {}", project_dir.display());
446	    eprintln!("  Code repo:    {code_repo}  (chid={code_chid_final})");
447	    eprintln!("  Session repo: {session_repo}  (chid={session_chid_final})");
448	    eprintln!(
449	        "  Symlink:      {} -> {}",
450	        plan.symlink_path.display(),
451	        plan.abs_target.display()
452	    );
453	
454	    Ok(())
455	}

12	pub fn chid(args: &ChidArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
13	    let c = &args.common;
14	    let spec = common::resolve_spec(c.pos_rev.as_deref(), c.pos_count, &c.revision, c.limit, "@");
15	    let hdr = common::resolve_header(&c.label, c.no_label);

18	        let (ids, anchor_index) =
19	            common::collect_ids(workspace, repo, &spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count)?;
20	
21	        for (i, commit_id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {

23	            let line = common::format_chid(&commit);
24	            if i == anchor_index {
25	                println!("{}", common::bold(&line));
26	            } else {
27	                println!("{line}");
28	            }
29	        }
30	        Ok(())
31	    })

> DEVELOPER

I'd like to tweak how you commit, push and finalize. Ask permission after preparing the commit's, then move the bookmarks and then ask permisison to "push the code" and "finalize the bot session". So I'm suggesting the last permissioned operation is:

git push --bookmark main -R . && vc-xw finalize --repo .claude ...

Make sense?

> AGENT

Makes sense. The flow would be:

1. Prepare both commits → present for approval
2. On approval, execute both `jj commit` commands + set bookmarks
3. Ask: "Push and finalize?"
4. On approval, `jj git push --bookmark main -R .` && `vc-x1 finalize ...` in one shot

That way you get two checkpoints — one before commits are locked in, one before anything leaves the machine. And the push + finalize are atomic from your perspective.

71	```
72	
73	- **Title**: target ~50 chars, short summary of *what* changed.
74	  Include the version. Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`,
75	  `test`, `docs`, `chore`.
76	- **Body**: expand on *what* if needed, plus short *why* and *how*.
77	- Examples:
78	  - `feat: add fix-ochid subcommand (0.22.0)`
79	  - `fix: fix-ochid prefix bug (0.22.1)`
80	  - `refactor: deduplicate common CLI flags (0.21.1)`
81	
82	## Pre-commit Requirements
83	
84	### User approval
85	
86	Never execute commit, squash, push, or finalize commands without the
87	user's explicit approval. Present changes for review first; only run
88	them after the user confirms. This applies to late changes too —
89	pause for review before squashing into an existing commit.
90	
91	### Notes references
92	
93	Multiple references must be separated: `[2],[3]` not `[2,3]` or `[2][3]`.
94	See [Todo format](notes/README.md#todo-format) for details.
95	
96	### Versioning
97	
98	Every change must start with a version bump. See
99	[Versioning during development](notes/README.md#versioning-during-development)
100	for details. Get user approval on single-step vs multi-step before starting.
101	
102	### Chores section headers
103	
104	Chores section headers use trailing version format:
105	
106	```
107	## Description (X.Y.Z)
108	```
109	
110	Example: `## Add `fn claude-symlink` (0.27.0)`
111	
112	### Pre-commit checklist
113	
114	Before proposing a commit, run all of the following and fix any issues:
115	
116	1. `cargo fmt`
117	2. `cargo clippy`
118	3. `cargo test`
119	4. `cargo install --path .` (if applicable)
120	5. Retest after install
121	6. Update `notes/todo.md` — add to `## Done` if completing a task
122	7. Update `notes/chores-*.md` — add a subsection describing the change
123	8. Update `notes/README.md` — if functionality changed (new flags,
124	   new subcommands, changed behavior)
125	
126	## ochid Trailers
127	
128	Every commit body must include an `ochid:` trailer pointing to the
129	counterpart commit in the other repo. The value is a workspace-root-relative
130	path followed by the changeID:
131	
132	- App repo commits point to `.claude`: `ochid: /.claude/<changeID>`
133	- Bot session commits point to app repo: `ochid: /<changeID>`
134	
135	Use `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` to get both changeIDs (first line
136	is app repo, second is `.claude`).
137	
138	## Session End Workflows
139	
```

```
138	## Session End Workflows
139	
140	When the user asks to "commit both repos" or says they're done, commit
141	both repos. Use the **same title** for both commits so they're easy to
142	correlate. The body can differ: the app repo body should summarize code
143	changes; the bot session repo body should note what was done in the
144	session.
145	
146	```
147	jj commit -m "shared title" -m "app body" -R .
148	jj commit -m "shared title" -m "session body" -R .claude
149	```
150	
151	After both commits, **pause and ask for user approval** before
152	proceeding to bookmark/push/finalize.
153	
154	When the user also asks to push, advance the current bookmark on both
155	repos, then push the app repo. Do **not** push `.claude` here —
156	`finalize` handles that push after squashing trailing writes.
157	
158	Replace `<bookmark>` with the active bookmark (e.g. `main`,
159	`dev-0.14.0`).
160	
161	```
162	jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r @- -R .
163	jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r @- -R .claude
164	jj git push --bookmark <bookmark> -R .
165	```
166	
167	### Late changes after push
168	
169	If changes are made to the app repo after it has been pushed (e.g.
170	updating CLAUDE.md or memory), the commit is now immutable. Use
171	`--ignore-immutable` to squash the changes in, then re-push:
172	
173	```
174	jj squash --ignore-immutable -R .
175	jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r @- -R .
176	jj git push --bookmark <bookmark> -R .
177	```
178	
179	### Finalize the .claude repo
180	
181	The **very last action** in a session is to finalize the `.claude` repo.
182	This squashes the working copy into the session commit and pushes. The
183	delay gives a safety margin against any pending writes. Always use a
184	short relative path for `--repo`.
185	
186	**Nothing should happen after finalize** — no memory writes, no tool
187	calls, no additional output. If any work is done after finalize, run
188	finalize again so the trailing writes are captured.
189	
190	`--bookmark` is required — use the active bookmark for the session.
191	
192	```
193	vc-x1 finalize --repo .claude --bookmark <bookmark> --delay 10 --detach --push
194	```
195	
196	Do **not** echo or restate the finalize output — the Bash tool
197	already displays it. Any trailing text output creates writes that
198	miss the finalize squash window.
199	
```

I like our --verbose technique we added to init, where "debug" is routed to stderr and use to stdout. I'd like that to be universal on all the commands, thoughts?

> AGENT

Agreed. It's a clean pattern — stdout for user-facing results, stderr for debug/diagnostic detail behind `--verbose`. Makes every command pipeable and scriptable.

For the existing read-only commands (`chid`, `desc`, `list`, `show`, `validate-desc`, `fix-desc`) the main output is already stdout. They just need a `--verbose` flag to optionally emit the diagnostic detail to stderr. Today they're pretty quiet anyway, so it might be more about establishing the convention now and filling in verbose output as needed.

For `clone`, `symlink`, and `finalize` the same split applies — progress on stdout, subprocess detail on stderr behind `--verbose`.

30	/// Run a command, printing it first. Returns stdout on success.
31	fn run(cmd: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
32	    let args_str = args.join(" ");
33	    eprintln!("  $ {cmd} {args_str}");
34	    let output = std::process::Command::new(cmd)
35	        .args(args)
36	        .current_dir(cwd)
37	        .output()
38	        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to run {cmd}: {e}"))?;
39	    if !output.status.success() {
40	        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
41	        return Err(format!("{cmd} {args_str} failed: {stderr}").into());
42	    }
43	    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())
44	}

46	/// Derive project name from a repo argument.
47	///
48	/// Handles: `owner/name`, `git@github.com:owner/name.git`,
49	/// `https://github.com/owner/name.git`, `https://github.com/owner/name`
50	fn derive_name(repo: &str) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
51	    // Strip trailing .git
52	    let repo = repo.strip_suffix(".git").unwrap_or(repo);
53	
54	    // Take everything after the last `/` or `:`
55	    let name = repo
56	        .rsplit_once('/')
57	        .or_else(|| repo.rsplit_once(':'))
58	        .map(|(_, name)| name)
59	        .unwrap_or(repo);
60	
61	    if name.is_empty() {
62	        return Err(format!("cannot derive project name from '{repo}'").into());
63	    }
64	    Ok(name.to_string())
65	}
66	
67	/// Resolve a repo argument to a git clone URL.
68	///
69	/// `owner/name` (no scheme, no `:` before `/`) becomes `git@github.com:owner/name.git`.
70	/// Anything else is passed through as-is.
71	fn resolve_url(repo: &str) -> String {
72	    // Already a URL (has scheme or SSH-style colon)
73	    if repo.contains("://") || repo.contains('@') {
74	        return repo.to_string();
75	    }

83	pub fn clone_repo(args: &CloneArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
84	    let parent_dir = match &args.dir {
85	        Some(d) => d.clone(),
86	        None => std::env::current_dir()?,
87	    };
88	
89	    let name = match &args.name {
90	        Some(n) => n.clone(),
91	        None => derive_name(&args.repo)?,
92	    };
93	    let project_dir = parent_dir.join(&name);
94	    let session_dir = project_dir.join(".claude");
95	    let url = resolve_url(&args.repo);
96	
97	    if args.dry_run {
98	        eprintln!("Dry run — would execute:");
99	        eprintln!("  1. git clone --recursive {url} {name}");
100	        eprintln!("  2. jj git init --colocate in {name}/");
101	        eprintln!("  3. jj git init --colocate in {name}/.claude/");
102	        eprintln!("  4. Create Claude Code symlink");
103	        return Ok(());
104	    }
105	
106	    // Preflight
107	    if project_dir.exists() {
108	        return Err(format!("'{}' already exists", project_dir.display()).into());
109	    }
110	
111	    std::process::Command::new("jj")
112	        .arg("--version")
113	        .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())
114	        .status()
115	        .map_err(|_| "jj is not installed")?;
116	
117	    // Step 1: git clone --recursive
118	    eprintln!("Cloning {url}...");
119	    let project_str = project_dir
120	        .to_str()
121	        .ok_or("project path is not valid UTF-8")?;
122	    run(
123	        "git",
124	        &["clone", "--recursive", &url, project_str],
125	        &parent_dir,
126	    )?;
127	
128	    // Step 2: jj git init --colocate in code repo
129	    eprintln!("\nInitializing jj in code repo...");
130	    run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &project_dir)?;
131	
132	    // Step 3: jj git init --colocate in session repo (if submodule exists)
133	    if session_dir.exists() {
134	        eprintln!("\nInitializing jj in session repo...");
135	        run("jj", &["git", "init", "--colocate"], &session_dir)?;
136	    } else {
137	        eprintln!("\nNote: no .claude submodule found — skipping session repo jj init");
138	    }
139	
140	    // Step 4: Create Claude Code symlink
141	    eprintln!("\nCreating Claude Code symlink...");
142	    let symlink_dir = {
143	        let home =
144	            std::env::var("HOME").map_err(|_| "HOME environment variable not set".to_string())?;
145	        PathBuf::from(home).join(".claude").join("projects")
146	    };
147	
148	    let meta = symlink::probe_symlink(
149	        &symlink_dir.join(symlink::encode_path(
150	            project_dir
151	                .to_str()
152	                .ok_or("project path is not valid UTF-8")?,
153	        )),
154	    );
155	    let plan = symlink::compute_plan(&project_dir, Path::new(".claude"), &symlink_dir, meta)?;
156	    symlink::execute_plan(&plan, false)?;
157	    eprintln!(
158	        "  Symlink: {} -> {}",
159	        plan.symlink_path.display(),
160	        plan.abs_target.display()
161	    );
162	
163	    eprintln!("\nDone! Project cloned to {}", project_dir.display());
164	    if args.verbose {
165	        eprintln!("  Code repo:    {project_str}");
166	        eprintln!("  Session repo: {}", session_dir.display());
167	    }
168	
169	    Ok(())

179	
180	    let symlink_dir = match &args.symlink_dir {
181	        Some(d) => d.clone(),
182	        None => {
183	            let home = std::env::var("HOME")
184	                .map_err(|_| "HOME environment variable not set".to_string())?;
185	            PathBuf::from(home).join(".claude").join("projects")
186	        }
187	    };
188	
189	    let abs_target = if target.is_absolute() {
190	        target.clone()
191	    } else {
192	        cwd.join(&target)
193	    };
194	
195	    let symlink_name = encode_path(
196	        cwd.to_str()
197	            .ok_or("current directory path is not valid UTF-8")?,
198	    );
199	    let symlink_path = symlink_dir.join(&symlink_name);
200	
201	    let meta = probe_symlink(&symlink_path);
202	    let plan = compute_plan(&cwd, &target, &symlink_dir, meta)?;
203	
204	    // Handle interactive prompt for replacement
205	    if let SymlinkAction::Replace { ref current_target } = plan.action {
206	        eprintln!(
207	            "Existing symlink: {} -> {}",
208	            plan.symlink_path.display(),
209	            current_target.display()
210	        );
211	        if !args.yes {
212	            eprint!("Replace with new target? [y/N] ");
213	            let mut response = String::new();
214	            std::io::stdin().read_line(&mut response)?;
215	            if !response.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case("y") {
216	                return Err("aborted".into());
217	            }
218	        }
219	    }
220	
221	    if plan.action == SymlinkAction::AlreadyCorrect {
222	        println!(
223	            "Already correct: {} -> {}",
224	            plan.symlink_path.display(),
225	            plan.abs_target.display()
226	        );
227	    } else {
228	        execute_plan(&plan, true)?;
229	        println!(
230	            "Created: {} -> {}",
231	            plan.symlink_path.display(),
232	            plan.abs_target.display()
233	        );
234	    }
235	
236	    if args.list {
237	        println!();
238	        println!("Contents of {}:", abs_target.display());
239	        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&abs_target)? {
240	            let entry = entry?;
241	            println!("  {}", entry.file_name().to_string_lossy());
242	        }
243	    }
244	
245	    Ok(())
246	}
```

Returns stdout on success.\nfn run(cmd: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let args_str = args.join(\" \");\n    eprintln!(\"  $ {cmd} {args_str}\");\n    let output = std::process::Command::new(cmd)\n        .args(args)\n        .current_dir(cwd)\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to run {cmd}: {e}\"))?;\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n        return Err(format!(\"{cmd} {args_str} failed: {stderr}\").into());\n    }\n    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Run a command. In verbose mode, prints the command with cwd, stdout, and stderr.\nfn run(\n    cmd: &str,\n    args: &[&str],\n    cwd: &Path,\n    verbose: bool,\n) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let args_str = args.join(\" \");\n    if verbose {\n        eprintln!(\"  {}$ {cmd} {args_str}\", cwd.display());\n    }\n    let output = std::process::Command::new(cmd)\n        .args(args)\n        .current_dir(cwd)\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to run {cmd}: {e}\"))?;\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();\n    if verbose {\n        if !stdout.is_empty() {\n            eprintln!(\"    stdout: {stdout}\");\n        }\n        if !stderr.is_empty() {\n            eprintln!(\"    stderr: {stderr}\");\n        }\n    }\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return Err(format!(\"{cmd} {args_str} failed: {stderr}\").into());\n    }\n    Ok(stdout)\n}"
}

> AGENT

Good eye. There are raw `Command::new` calls in:

- **init.rs**: `jj_chid()` (line 79), `gh_whoami()` (line 103), `gh_repo_exists()` (line 117), and two preflight checks (lines 170, 181)
- **clone.rs**: one preflight check (line 98)
- **finalize.rs**: two calls (its own thing with `--log`)

The preflight checks are fire-and-forget (just checking exit status, no output needed). `jj_chid` and `gh_whoami`/`gh_repo_exists` are silent helpers that don't want verbose output. So they're different enough from `run()` that forcing them through it would add noise.

That said, `jj_chid()` could use `run()` with `verbose=false` and just extract the output. Same for `gh_whoami`. Worth doing or leave them?

1. `jj_chid()` → `run("jj", ..., verbose=false)`

Now let me refactor them all. The tricky ones:

- `gh_repo_exists` returns `bool` — `run()` returns `Err` on failure, so `Ok(run(...).is_ok())`
- `jj_chid` needs to truncate the output to 12 chars
- Preflight checks need cwd — I'll use `"."` since they don't care

  "old_string": "/// Get the short (12-char) jj change ID for a revision, without printing.\nfn jj_chid(rev: &str, cwd: &Path) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let output = std::process::Command::new(\"jj\")\n        .args([\n            \"log\",\n            \"-r\",\n            rev,\n            \"--no-graph\",\n            \"-T\",\n            \"change_id\",\n            \"--limit\",\n            \"1\",\n        ])\n        .current_dir(cwd)\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to run jj: {e}\"))?;\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n        return Err(format!(\"jj log failed: {stderr}\").into());\n    }\n    let full = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();\n    Ok(full[..full.len().min(12)].to_string())\n}\n\n/// Get the current GitHub user via `gh api user`.\nfn gh_whoami() -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let output = std::process::Command::new(\"gh\")\n        .args([\"api\", \"user\", \"--jq\", \".login\"])\n        .output()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to run gh: {e}\"))?;\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n        return Err(format!(\"gh api user failed (is gh authenticated?): {stderr}\").into());\n    }\n    Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())\n}\n\n/// Check if a GitHub repo exists.\nfn gh_repo_exists(owner: &str, name: &str) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let full = format!(\"{owner}/{name}\");\n    let output = std::process::Command::new(\"gh\")\n        .args([\"repo\", \"view\", &full])\n        .stdout(std::process::Stdio::null())\n        .stderr(std::process::Stdio::null())\n        .status()\n        .map_err(|e| format!(\"failed to run gh: {e}\"))?;\n    Ok(output.success())\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Get the short (12-char) jj change ID for a revision, without printing.\nfn jj_chid(rev: &str, cwd: &Path) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let full = run(\n        \"jj\",\n        &[\"log\", \"-r\", rev, \"--no-graph\", \"-T\", \"change_id\", \"--limit\", \"1\"],\n        cwd,\n        false,\n    )?;\n    Ok(full[..full.len().min(12)].to_string())\n}\n\n/// Get the current GitHub user via `gh api user`.\nfn gh_whoami() -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    run(\"gh\", &[\"api\", \"user\", \"--jq\", \".login\"], Path::new(\".\"), false)\n}\n\n/// Check if a GitHub repo exists.\nfn gh_repo_exists(owner: &str, name: &str) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let full = format!(\"{owner}/{name}\");\n    Ok(run(\"gh\", &[\"repo\", \"view\", &full], Path::new(\".\"), false).is_ok())\n}"
}

> DEVELOPER

Hmm, we have finalize::log_msg and use it extensively in finalize and invoke it 3 times in main, seems that could be used more universally. Thoughts? (note when I say "Thoughts" I want to discuss what should/could be done and generally don't want you to do it)

> AGENT

`finalize::log_msg` writes timestamped entries to an optional log file — it's a diagnostic/tracing mechanism for debugging finalize's async detach flow. It's not really the same concern as `--verbose` stderr output.

I see two separate things:

1. **`--verbose` stderr** (what we just did): real-time diagnostic output for the user watching the terminal
2. **File-based logging** (what `log_msg` does): persistent trace for post-mortem debugging, especially useful when the process detaches and there's no terminal

They could converge — e.g. a shared logging facility that writes to stderr when verbose and optionally to a file when `--log` is specified. But that's a bigger design decision. Right now `log_msg` is tightly coupled to finalize's detach semantics (PID tracking, nanosecond timestamps for ordering).

A lighter touch: make `log_msg` available in `common.rs` so any command *could* use it with `--log`, without forcing it. But I'm not sure the other commands need file logging — they run in the foreground where stderr is sufficient.

What's your thinking — is there a case where you'd want `--log` on init or clone?

> DEVELOPER

I see the difference, but if we adopted log_msg instead of eprintln the user wouldn't redirects it fees more direct. It would also allow for "levels" although maybe we should use a "debugging" crate instead of log_msg?

> AGENT

Good thinking. The progression is:

1. **Current `log_msg`**: manual file logging, no levels, finalize-only
2. **Roll our own**: move `log_msg` to common, add levels — but we'd be reinventing the wheel
3. **Use a crate**: `tracing` or `log` + a backend — levels, filtering, output targets all handled

The Rust ecosystem standard is `tracing` (or the simpler `log` facade). With `tracing`:
- `tracing::info!("Step 1: Creating directories...")` → stdout in normal mode
- `tracing::debug!("git init in {}", dir)` → stderr with `--verbose`
- `tracing::trace!("stdout: {}", output)` → file with `--log`
- Finalize's detach logging just becomes another subscriber writing to a file

The nice part: we'd replace both `println!` (progress), `eprintln!` (verbose), and `log_msg` (file) with one unified system. Level filtering handles which output goes where.

The downside: it's a dependency and some setup boilerplate for the subscriber config. And `tracing` might be overkill for a CLI this size — `log` + `env_logger` is lighter.

Worth exploring, but feels like its own task rather than part of 0.29.0. Add it as a todo?

> DEVELOPER

We've commited and pushed 0.29.0 so this is actually 0.30.0 and currently is a "run" and "log" cleanup at this stage. We could commit waht we've got so far and make 0.31.0 adopting a new logging scheme?

> AGENT

Makes sense. So:

- **0.30.0**: what we have now — `--verbose` on all commands, `common::run()` refactor, `chid` bold removal, CLAUDE.md two-checkpoint workflow
- **0.31.0**: adopt `tracing` (or `log`) to unify `println!`/`eprintln!`/`log_msg` into one system

Want me to bump to 0.30.0 and prepare the commit?

done

> DEVELOPER

I asked google "what is the 'best' logging/tracing crate for rust code" the short answer was `tracing` for "Production/Async" and `log` for "libraries" and `env-logger` for "Prototypes/CLI". It mentioned a few other specialized choices `log4rs`, `fern`, `slog` (old), and `defmt` (embedded). env_logger only supporting via environment variable is not attractive, I'd like that as a choice but type `RUST_LOG=info` is not great compared to -l=1 or -li if we control it at the argument level. Thoughts

> AGENT

Agreed. `env_logger` being env-var-only is awkward for a CLI tool. The user shouldn't need `RUST_LOG=debug vc-x1 init ...` when `-v` is right there.

I think the right approach is:

- **`log`** as the facade — it's the standard trait, lightweight, and what libraries expect
- **A thin custom subscriber** that routes based on our CLI flags, not env vars

The subscriber would be ~20 lines:
- `info!` and above → stdout (step headers, results)
- `debug!` → stderr (only when `--verbose`)
- `trace!` → file (only when `--log <path>`)
- `error!`/`warn!` → stderr always

This replaces `println!`, `eprintln!`, and `log_msg` with one system. The CLI flags we already have (`--verbose`, `--log`) drive it — no env vars needed.

We could also allow `RUST_LOG` as a fallback override for power users, but the primary interface is the flags.

`tracing` would work too but it's heavier and the async/span features aren't useful for us. `log` is simpler and sufficient.

Does that direction sound right?

> DEVELOPER

yes, but one thing I'd prefer is to be able to have the level be a parameter log(info, "..."). Ideally I'd like to turn on logging from the command line for a specific library or a routine in a specific library. Maybe asking to much, LoL.

> AGENT

Not asking too much — that's exactly what `log`'s filtering gives you. The `log` crate already does `log::info!("...")`, `log::debug!("...")` etc., and the filter targets are module paths:

```
# Everything at info, but init.rs at debug
vc-x1 init my-project -v init

# Or maybe
vc-x1 init my-project --log-filter "vc_x1::init=debug,vc_x1::clone=trace"
```

The `env_filter` crate (from the `tracing` ecosystem but works with `log` too) parses exactly this syntax: `module::path=level`. We'd just wire it to a CLI flag instead of an env var.

So the interface could be:

- `-v` / `--verbose` — shorthand for "everything at debug on stderr"
- `--log-filter "vc_x1::init=debug"` — fine-grained per-module control
- `--log <path>` — also write to a file (for finalize's detach case)
- `RUST_LOG` — fallback for power users, lowest priority

The `log` macros already embed the module path automatically — `log::debug!("foo")` in `src/init.rs` gets tagged as `vc_x1::init`. So per-module filtering comes for free.

The piece we'd write: a small subscriber that reads our CLI flags, builds a filter, and routes output to stdout/stderr/file based on level. Maybe 50-80 lines.

Sound like the right scope for 0.31.0?

> DEVELOPER

But log::debug! is compile time I'd like log(enabled, ...) and then `enabled` is maybe a thread local variable so a particular line in a particluar function on a particular thread could be enabled at runtime! Now I'm probably asking for the universe, Lol!

> AGENT

Not the universe — but definitely custom territory. The `log` crate does have runtime filtering (the `log::log!` macro checks a runtime level), but it's per-module, not per-line or per-thread.

What you're describing is more like:

```rust
// Each log site has an ID that can be toggled at runtime
log_point!(LP_INIT_STEP5, "ochid cross-reference: {}", chid);
```

Where `LP_INIT_STEP5` is a runtime-mutable flag, addressable by name from the CLI. Think DTrace probes or Linux tracepoints — individually switchable instrumentation points.

That's beyond what `log`, `tracing`, or any standard Rust crate does out of the box. `tracing` gets closest with its span/event system, but per-callsite runtime toggling with thread granularity is bespoke.

For 0.31.0 I'd suggest:

1. **Start with `log` + per-module runtime filtering** — covers 90% of use cases, standard ecosystem, small effort
2. **Note the per-line/per-thread vision as a future goal** — maybe 0.32.0 or later, possibly as a custom `LogPoint` system built on top of `log`

The per-module filtering already lets you do "show me only what init is doing" which is the most common debugging scenario. The per-line stuff would be powerful but is a design project in itself.

Want to start 0.31.0 with the pragmatic approach?

> DEVELOPER

Great suggestion, capture this conversation and the suggestion 1 & 2 todo+chores and let's do 1 as 0.31.0 and 2 maybe someday.

{
  "file_path": "/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1/src/logging.rs",
  "content": "use std::io::Write;\nuse std::sync::Mutex;\n\nuse log::{Level, Log, Metadata, Record};\n\n/// Simple logger that routes by level:\n/// - info and above → stdout (user-facing progress)\n/// - debug → stderr (only when verbose)\n/// - trace → stderr (only when verbose)\n/// - warn/error → stderr (always)\npub struct CliLogger {\n    verbose: bool,\n    log_file: Option<Mutex<std::fs::File>>,\n}\n\nimpl CliLogger {\n    pub fn new(verbose: bool, log_path: Option<&str>) -> Self {\n        let log_file = log_path.map(|path| {\n            Mutex::new(\n                std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n                    .create(true)\n                    .append(true)\n                    .open(path)\n                    .expect(\"failed to open log file\"),\n            )\n        });\n        CliLogger { verbose, log_file }\n    }\n\n    /// Initialize as the global logger.\n    pub fn init(verbose: bool, log_path: Option<&str>) {\n        let logger = Box::new(CliLogger::new(verbose, log_path));\n        log::set_max_level(if verbose {\n            log::LevelFilter::Debug\n        } else {\n            log::LevelFilter::Info\n        });\n        log::set_boxed_logger(logger).expect(\"failed to set logger\");\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Log for CliLogger {\n    fn enabled(&self, metadata: &Metadata) -> bool {\n        match metadata.level() {\n            Level::Error | Level::Warn => true,\n            Level::Info => true,\n            Level::Debug | Level::Trace => self.verbose,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn log(&self, record: &Record) {\n        if !self.enabled(record.metadata()) {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        let msg = format!(\"{}\", record.args());\n\n        // Write to log file if configured\n        if let Some(ref file) = self.log_file {\n            if let Ok(mut f) = file.lock() {\n                let _ = writeln!(f, \"[{}] {}: {}\", record.level(), record.target(), msg);\n            }\n        }\n\n        match record.level() {\n            // User-facing progress → stdout\n            Level::Info => println!(\"{msg}\"),\n            // Errors and warnings → stderr always\n            Level::Error => eprintln!(\"error: {msg}\"),\n            Level::Warn => eprintln!(\"warn: {msg}\"),\n            // Debug/trace → stderr (only reached if verbose, checked in enabled())\n            Level::Debug | Level::Trace => eprintln!(\"{msg}\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self) {\n        use std::io;\n        let _ = io::stdout().flush();\n        let _ = io::stderr().flush();\n        if let Some(ref file) = self.log_file {\n            if let Ok(mut f) = file.lock() {\n                let _ = f.flush();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n"
}

163	/// Run a shell command. In verbose mode, prints the command with cwd, stdout, and stderr
164	/// to stderr. In normal mode, only prints on failure. Returns stdout on success.
165	pub fn run(
166	    cmd: &str,
167	    args: &[&str],
168	    cwd: &Path,
169	    verbose: bool,
170	) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
171	    let args_str = args.join(" ");
172	    if verbose {
173	        eprintln!("  {}$ {cmd} {args_str}", cwd.display());
174	    }
175	    let output = std::process::Command::new(cmd)
176	        .args(args)
177	        .current_dir(cwd)
178	        .output()
179	        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to run {cmd}: {e}"))?;
180	    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();
181	    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();
182	    if verbose {
183	        if !stdout.is_empty() {
184	            eprintln!("    stdout: {stdout}");
185	        }
186	        if !stderr.is_empty() {
187	            eprintln!("    stderr: {stderr}");
188	        }
189	    }
190	    if !output.status.success() {
191	        return Err(format!("{cmd} {args_str} failed: {stderr}").into());
192	    }
193	    Ok(stdout)
194	}

44	fn run_retry(
45	    cmd: &str,
46	    args: &[&str],
47	    cwd: &Path,
48	    retries: u32,
49	    delay_secs: u64,
50	    verbose: bool,

> DEVELOPER

Explain where the `a` parameter comes from in:
impl Commands {
    fn verbose(&self) -> bool {
        match self {
            Commands::Chid(a) => a.common.verbose,
            Commands::Desc(a) => a.common.verbose,
            Commands::List(a) => a.common.verbose,
            Commands::Show(a) => a.common.verbose,
            Commands::ValidateDesc(a) => a.verbose,
            Commands::FixDesc(a) => a.verbose,
            Commands::Clone(a) => a.verbose,
            Commands::Init(a) => a.verbose,
            Commands::Symlink(a) => a.verbose,
            Commands::Finalize(_) => false, // finalize uses --log
        }
    }
}

> AGENT

`a` is a pattern binding in the `match` arm. Each `Commands` variant holds a struct — e.g. `Commands::Init(init::InitArgs)`. When you write:

```rust
Commands::Init(a) => a.verbose,
```

Rust destructures the enum variant and binds the inner `InitArgs` value to `a`. It's the same as:

```rust
Commands::Init(args) => args.verbose,
```

The name `a` is arbitrary — I used it for brevity. `_` on the `Finalize` arm means "ignore the inner value, don't bind it."

> DEVELOPER

So here verbose is being invoked:
    logging::CliLogger::init(cli.command.verbose(), None);

So `a` is `cli` from `let cli = Cli::parse()` and cli is an instance of `struct Cli` which is then matched against what command the user passed, Chid, Desc, ...

> AGENT

Exactly. `cli.command` is the `Commands` enum, and `.verbose()` matches on which variant it is to extract the `verbose` field from whichever args struct is inside. So the chain is:

```
cli (Cli) → .command (Commands::Init(InitArgs)) → .verbose() matches Init(a) → a.verbose
```

> DEVELOPER

so `a` == `self` which isa `cli.command` which is of tyope Commands

> AGENT

Close but one level deeper. `self` is the `Commands` enum. `a` is what's *inside* the variant — the args struct. So:

- `self` == `cli.command` == `Commands::Init(InitArgs { ... })`
- `a` == the `InitArgs { ... }` inside it

The `match` unwraps the enum to get at the inner value.

> DEVELOPER

I think so to, now when I hover over one of the, chid_args it says `let chids_args: &ChidArgs` so it now reads what it is, a just meant nothing I didn't even connect it with "args" in isolation. Is this a suggested naming technique in the rust community?

> AGENT

Not a formal convention, but it's common practice. The Rust community favors descriptive names — the official style guide says variables should be `snake_case` and meaningful. You'll see both patterns in the wild:

- **Short/generic**: `a`, `args`, `x` — common in quick closures, iterators, or when the type is obvious from context
- **Descriptive**: `init_args`, `commit_id`, `session_dir` — preferred when the type alone doesn't tell the full story

The Rust compiler and rust-analyzer (the LSP) show the type on hover, so some people lean on that and use shorter names. But for code you'll read months later — or that someone else will read — descriptive wins.

Your instinct is right: if you have to think about what `a` means, it should have a better name.

The match arms in `main` are repetitive — same pattern 9 times:

```rust
Commands::Foo(args) => {
    if let Err(e) = foo::foo(&args) {
        eprintln!("error: {e}");
        return ExitCode::FAILURE;
    }
    ExitCode::SUCCESS
}
```

Now that we have `log`, those `eprintln!("error: {e}")` should become `log::error!("{e}")`. But beyond that, the boilerplate could be a helper:

```rust
fn run_command(result: Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>) -> ExitCode {
    match result {
        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
        Err(e) => {
            log::error!("{e}");
            ExitCode::FAILURE
        }
    }
}
```

Then each arm becomes one line:

```rust
Commands::Init(args) => run_command(init::init(&args)),
Commands::Clone(args) => run_command(clone::clone_repo(&args)),
```

Finalize would be the only special case (it has `log_msg` calls around it).

That's cleaner — one system, not two. The convention:

- `info!` → stdout, no indent, always shown (user-facing progress/results)
- `warn!` → stderr, always shown
- `error!` → stderr, always shown
- `debug!` → stderr, indented, `--verbose` only
- `trace!` → stderr, indented, `--verbose` or `--log` only

No raw `println!` or `eprintln!` anywhere except maybe interactive prompts (like symlink's "Replace? [y/N]"). Everything goes through `log`, the logger handles routing and indentation.

One option: don't log the prompt until *after* the response, then log them together:

```rust

```

The user sees the prompt with their cursor inline (via raw `eprint!`), and the log gets `Replace with new target? [y/N] y` as one line.

1	use std::io::Write;
2	use std::sync::Mutex;
3	
4	use log::{Level, Log, Metadata, Record};
5	
6	/// Simple logger that routes by level:
7	/// - info and above → stdout (user-facing progress)
8	/// - debug → stderr (only when verbose)
9	/// - trace → stderr (only when verbose)
10	/// - warn/error → stderr (always)
11	pub struct CliLogger {
12	    verbose: bool,
13	    log_file: Option<Mutex<std::fs::File>>,
14	}
15	
16	impl CliLogger {
17	    pub fn new(verbose: bool, log_path: Option<&str>) -> Self {
18	        let log_file = log_path.map(|path| {
19	            Mutex::new(
20	                std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
21	                    .create(true)
22	                    .append(true)
23	                    .open(path)
24	                    .expect("failed to open log file"),
25	            )
26	        });
27	        CliLogger { verbose, log_file }
28	    }
29	
30	    /// Initialize as the global logger.
31	    pub fn init(verbose: bool, log_path: Option<&str>) {
32	        let logger = Box::new(CliLogger::new(verbose, log_path));
33	        log::set_max_level(if verbose {
34	            log::LevelFilter::Debug
35	        } else {
36	            log::LevelFilter::Info
37	        });
38	        log::set_boxed_logger(logger).expect("failed to set logger");
39	    }
40	}
41	
42	impl Log for CliLogger {
43	    fn enabled(&self, metadata: &Metadata) -> bool {
44	        match metadata.level() {
45	            Level::Error | Level::Warn => true,
46	            Level::Info => true,
47	            Level::Debug | Level::Trace => self.verbose,
48	        }
49	    }
50	
51	    fn log(&self, record: &Record) {
52	        if !self.enabled(record.metadata()) {
53	            return;
54	        }
55	
56	        let msg = format!("{}", record.args());
57	
58	        // Write to log file if configured
59	        if let Some(ref file) = self.log_file
60	            && let Ok(mut f) = file.lock()
61	        {
62	            let _ = writeln!(f, "[{}] {}: {}", record.level(), record.target(), msg);
63	        }
64	
65	        match record.level() {
66	            // User-facing progress → stdout
67	            Level::Info => println!("{msg}"),
68	            // Errors and warnings → stderr always
69	            Level::Error => eprintln!("error: {msg}"),
70	            Level::Warn => eprintln!("warn: {msg}"),
71	            // Debug/trace → stderr (only reached if verbose, checked in enabled())
72	            Level::Debug | Level::Trace => eprintln!("{msg}"),
73	        }
74	    }
75	
76	    fn flush(&self) {
77	        use std::io;
78	        let _ = io::stdout().flush();
79	        let _ = io::stderr().flush();
80	        if let Some(ref file) = self.log_file
81	            && let Ok(mut f) = file.lock()
82	        {
83	            let _ = f.flush();
84	        }
85	    }
86	}
87

163	/// Run a shell command. Logs the command and output at debug level.
164	/// Returns stdout on success.
165	pub fn run(cmd: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
166	    let args_str = args.join(" ");
167	    log::debug!("  {}$ {cmd} {args_str}", cwd.display());
168	    let output = std::process::Command::new(cmd)
169	        .args(args)
170	        .current_dir(cwd)
171	        .output()
172	        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to run {cmd}: {e}"))?;
173	    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();
174	    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();
175	    if !stdout.is_empty() {
176	        log::debug!("    stdout: {stdout}");
177	    }
178	    if !stderr.is_empty() {
179	        log::debug!("    stderr: {stderr}");
180	    }
181	    if !output.status.success() {
182	        return Err(format!("{cmd} {args_str} failed: {stderr}").into());
183	    }
184	    Ok(stdout)
185	}
186

42	
43	/// Run a command with retries, sleeping between attempts.
44	fn run_retry(
45	    cmd: &str,
46	    args: &[&str],
47	    cwd: &Path,
48	    retries: u32,
49	    delay_secs: u64,
50	) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
51	    let mut last_err = String::new();
52	    for attempt in 1..=retries {
53	        match run(cmd, args, cwd) {
54	            Ok(out) => {
55	                if attempt > 1 {
56	                    debug!("  succeeded after {attempt} attempts");
57	                }
58	                return Ok(out);
59	            }
60	            Err(e) => {
61	                last_err = e.to_string();
62	                if attempt < retries {
63	                    debug!("  attempt {attempt}/{retries} failed: {last_err}");
64	                    debug!("  retrying in {delay_secs}s...");
65	                    std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(delay_secs));
66	                }
67	            }
68	        }
69	    }
70	    Err(format!("failed after {retries} attempts: {last_err}").into())
71	}
```

> AGENT

Good point — it keeps everything visible through one system. In verbose mode you'd see `$ mkdir -p ...` and `$ tee ...` (or similar) instead of silent Rust calls.

But `mkdir -p` maps cleanly to `create_dir_all`. For writing files, there's no clean single-command equivalent — `tee` or `echo >` would work but feel hacky. We could use a small helper like `write_file()` that logs what it's doing at debug level without shelling out:

```rust
log::debug!("writing {}", path.display());
std::fs::write(path, content)?;
```

That gives visibility without the overhead of shelling out for file writes. For mkdir, `run("mkdir", &["-p", ...])` is fine.

Mix of both? `run` for commands, `log::debug!` + `std::fs::write` for file I/O? Or shell out for everything?

You're right — the `debug!` + `std::fs::write` pairs are verbose in the source compared to the clean `run()` calls. Two options:

1. **Small helpers** like `debug_write(path, content)` and `debug_mkdir(path)` that log + do the operation in one call
2. **Just inline the debug in the helper** — e.g. `fs_write(path, content)` that does `log::debug!("write {}", path.display()); std::fs::write(path, content)`

Then step 3 becomes:

```rust
fs_write(&project_dir.join(".vc-config.toml"), VC_CONFIG_CODE)?;
fs_write(&project_dir.join(".gitignore"), GITIGNORE_CODE)?;
```

Actually, there's no clean single shell command for "write this content to a file." You'd need something like:

```rust
run("sh", &["-c", &format!("cat > .vc-config.toml << 'EOF'\n{VC_CONFIG_CODE}EOF")], &project_dir)?;
```

That's ugly. `run()` is designed for commands with args, not for piping content into files. The helper approach is cleaner.

29	    path.replace(['/', '.'], "-")

32	/// Compute the symlink plan without performing any I/O.
33	///
34	/// # Arguments
35	/// * `cwd` — current working directory (used to derive the symlink name)
36	/// * `target` — the directory the symlink should point to (resolved to absolute)
37	/// * `symlink_dir` — parent directory for the symlink (e.g. `~/.claude/projects`)
38	/// * `target_exists` — whether the target directory exists on disk
39	/// * `symlink_meta` — what currently exists at the symlink path:
40	///   - `None` — nothing exists
41	///   - `Some(None)` — exists but is not a symlink (file or directory)
42	///   - `Some(Some(path))` — existing symlink pointing to `path`
43	pub fn compute_plan(
44	    cwd: &Path,
45	    target: &Path,
46	    symlink_dir: &Path,
47	    symlink_meta: Option<Option<PathBuf>>,
48	) -> Result<SymlinkPlan, String> {
49	    // Resolve target to absolute path
50	    let abs_target = if target.is_absolute() {
51	        target.to_path_buf()
52	    } else {
53	        cwd.join(target)
54	    };
55	
56	    // Derive symlink name from cwd
57	    let cwd_str = cwd
58	        .to_str()
59	        .ok_or_else(|| "current directory path is not valid UTF-8".to_string())?;
60	    let symlink_name = encode_path(cwd_str);
61	    let symlink_path = symlink_dir.join(symlink_name);
62	
63	    let action = match symlink_meta {
64	        None => SymlinkAction::Create,
65	        Some(None) => {
66	            return Err(format!(
67	                "'{}' exists and is not a symlink",
68	                symlink_path.display()
69	            ));
70	        }
71	        Some(Some(current_target)) => {
72	            if current_target == abs_target {
73	                SymlinkAction::AlreadyCorrect
74	            } else {
75	                SymlinkAction::Replace { current_target }
76	            }
77	        }
78	    };
79	
80	    Ok(SymlinkPlan {
81	        abs_target,
82	        symlink_path,
83	        action,
84	    })
85	}

87	/// Read what exists at a path without following symlinks.
88	///
89	/// Returns:
90	/// - `None` — nothing exists
91	/// - `Some(None)` — exists but is not a symlink
92	/// - `Some(Some(target))` — symlink pointing to target
93	pub fn probe_symlink(path: &Path) -> Option<Option<PathBuf>> {
94	    match path.symlink_metadata() {
95	        Err(_) => None,
96	        Ok(meta) => {
97	            if meta.is_symlink() {

100	                Some(None)
101	            }
102	        }
103	    }
104	}

106	/// Execute a symlink plan: create the target dir if needed, create/replace the symlink.
107	pub fn execute_plan(plan: &SymlinkPlan, create_target: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
108	    if create_target && !plan.abs_target.exists() {
109	        std::fs::create_dir_all(&plan.abs_target)
110	            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot create target '{}': {e}", plan.abs_target.display()))?;
111	    }
112	
113	    // Ensure symlink parent directory exists
114	    if let Some(parent) = plan.symlink_path.parent() {
115	        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| {
116	            format!(
117	                "cannot create symlink directory '{}': {e}",
118	                parent.display()
119	            )
120	        })?;
121	    }
122	
123	    match &plan.action {
124	        SymlinkAction::Create => {}
125	        SymlinkAction::Replace { .. } => {
126	            std::fs::remove_file(&plan.symlink_path).map_err(|e| {
127	                format!(
128	                    "cannot remove existing symlink '{}': {e}",
129	                    plan.symlink_path.display()
130	                )
131	            })?;
132	        }
133	        SymlinkAction::AlreadyCorrect => return Ok(()),
134	    }
135	
136	    #[cfg(unix)]
137	    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&plan.abs_target, &plan.symlink_path).map_err(|e| {
138	        format!(
139	            "cannot create symlink '{}' -> '{}': {e}",
140	            plan.symlink_path.display(),
141	            plan.abs_target.display()
142	        )
143	    })?;
144	
145	    #[cfg(not(unix))]
146	    return Err("symlink creation is only supported on Unix".to_string());
147	
148	    Ok(())
149	}

11	    Replace { current_target: PathBuf },
12	    /// The symlink already points to the correct target — nothing to do.
13	    AlreadyCorrect,
14	}

16	/// The result of planning a symlink operation.
17	#[derive(Debug)]
18	pub struct SymlinkPlan {
19	    /// Absolute path to the target directory (what the symlink points to).
20	    pub abs_target: PathBuf,
21	    /// Full path of the symlink to create/replace.
22	    pub symlink_path: PathBuf,
23	    /// What action is needed.
24	    pub action: SymlinkAction,
25	}
26	
27	/// Encode a path the way Claude Code does: replace `/` and `.` with `-`.
28	pub fn encode_path(path: &str) -> String {
29	    path.replace(['/', '.'], "-")
30	}
31	
32	/// Compute the symlink plan without performing any I/O.
33	///
34	/// # Arguments
35	/// * `cwd` — current working directory (used to derive the symlink name)
36	/// * `target` — the directory the symlink should point to (resolved to absolute)
37	/// * `symlink_dir` — parent directory for the symlink (e.g. `~/.claude/projects`)
38	/// * `target_exists` — whether the target directory exists on disk
39	/// * `symlink_meta` — what currently exists at the symlink path:
40	///   - `None` — nothing exists
41	///   - `Some(None)` — exists but is not a symlink (file or directory)
42	///   - `Some(Some(path))` — existing symlink pointing to `path`
43	pub fn compute_plan(
44	    cwd: &Path,
45	    target: &Path,
46	    symlink_dir: &Path,
47	    symlink_meta: Option<Option<PathBuf>>,
48	) -> Result<SymlinkPlan, String> {
49	    // Resolve target to absolute path
50	    let abs_target = if target.is_absolute() {
51	        target.to_path_buf()
52	    } else {
53	        cwd.join(target)
54	    };
55	
56	    // Derive symlink name from cwd
57	    let cwd_str = cwd
58	        .to_str()
59	        .ok_or_else(|| "current directory path is not valid UTF-8".to_string())?;
60	    let symlink_name = encode_path(cwd_str);
61	    let symlink_path = symlink_dir.join(symlink_name);
62	
63	    let action = match symlink_meta {
64	        None => SymlinkAction::Create,
65	        Some(None) => {
66	            return Err(format!(
67	                "'{}' exists and is not a symlink",
68	                symlink_path.display()
69	            ));
70	        }
71	        Some(Some(current_target)) => {
72	            if current_target == abs_target {
73	                SymlinkAction::AlreadyCorrect
74	            } else {
75	                SymlinkAction::Replace { current_target }
76	            }
77	        }
78	    };
79	
80	    Ok(SymlinkPlan {
81	        abs_target,
82	        symlink_path,
83	        action,
84	    })
85	}

87	/// Read what exists at a path without following symlinks.
88	///
89	/// Returns:
90	/// - `None` — nothing exists
91	/// - `Some(None)` — exists but is not a symlink
92	/// - `Some(Some(target))` — symlink pointing to target
93	pub fn probe_symlink(path: &Path) -> Option<Option<PathBuf>> {
94	    match path.symlink_metadata() {
95	        Err(_) => None,
96	        Ok(meta) => {
97	            if meta.is_symlink() {
98	                Some(Some(std::fs::read_link(path).unwrap_or_default()))
99	            } else {
100	                Some(None)
101	            }
102	        }
103	    }
104	}

106	/// Execute a symlink plan: create the target dir if needed, create/replace the symlink.
107	pub fn execute_plan(plan: &SymlinkPlan, create_target: bool) -> Result<(), String> {
108	    if create_target && !plan.abs_target.exists() {
109	        std::fs::create_dir_all(&plan.abs_target)
110	            .map_err(|e| format!("cannot create target '{}': {e}", plan.abs_target.display()))?;
111	    }
112	
113	    // Ensure symlink parent directory exists
114	    if let Some(parent) = plan.symlink_path.parent() {
115	        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| {
116	            format!(
117	                "cannot create symlink directory '{}': {e}",
118	                parent.display()
119	            )
120	        })?;
121	    }
122	
123	    match &plan.action {
124	        SymlinkAction::Create => {}
125	        SymlinkAction::Replace { .. } => {
126	            std::fs::remove_file(&plan.symlink_path).map_err(|e| {
127	                format!(
128	                    "cannot remove existing symlink '{}': {e}",
129	                    plan.symlink_path.display()
130	                )
131	            })?;
132	        }
133	        SymlinkAction::AlreadyCorrect => return Ok(()),
134	    }
135	
136	    #[cfg(unix)]
137	    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&plan.abs_target, &plan.symlink_path).map_err(|e| {
138	        format!(
139	            "cannot create symlink '{}' -> '{}': {e}",
140	            plan.symlink_path.display(),
141	            plan.abs_target.display()
142	        )
143	    })?;
144	
145	    #[cfg(not(unix))]
146	    return Err("symlink creation is only supported on Unix".to_string());
147	
148	    Ok(())
149	}

153	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
154	pub struct SymlinkArgs {
155	    /// Directory to link to [default: .claude]
156	    #[arg(value_name = "TARGET")]
157	    pub target: Option<String>,
158	
159	    /// Directory for symlink [default: ~/.claude/projects]
160	    #[arg(long, value_name = "PATH")]
161	    pub symlink_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
162	
163	    /// List contents of symlinked directory after creation
164	    #[arg(short, long)]
165	    pub list: bool,
166	
167	    /// Replace existing symlink without prompting
168	    #[arg(short, long)]
169	    pub yes: bool,
170	
171	    /// Verbose output (diagnostic detail on stderr)
172	    #[arg(short, long)]
173	    pub verbose: bool,
174	}
175	
176	pub fn symlink(args: &SymlinkArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
177	    let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
178	
179	    let target = match &args.target {
180	        Some(t) => PathBuf::from(t),
181	        None => PathBuf::from(".claude"),
182	    };
183	
184	    let symlink_dir = match &args.symlink_dir {
185	        Some(d) => d.clone(),
186	        None => {
187	            let home = std::env::var("HOME")
188	                .map_err(|_| "HOME environment variable not set".to_string())?;
189	            PathBuf::from(home).join(".claude").join("projects")
190	        }
191	    };
192	
193	    let abs_target = if target.is_absolute() {
194	        target.clone()
195	    } else {
196	        cwd.join(&target)
197	    };
198	
199	    let symlink_name = encode_path(
200	        cwd.to_str()
201	            .ok_or("current directory path is not valid UTF-8")?,
202	    );
203	    let symlink_path = symlink_dir.join(&symlink_name);
204	
205	    let meta = probe_symlink(&symlink_path);
206	    let plan = compute_plan(&cwd, &target, &symlink_dir, meta)?;
207	
208	    // Handle interactive prompt for replacement
209	    if let SymlinkAction::Replace { ref current_target } = plan.action {
210	        log::info!(
211	            "Existing symlink: {} -> {}",
212	            plan.symlink_path.display(),
213	            current_target.display()
214	        );
215	        if !args.yes {
216	            let response = crate::common::prompt("Replace with new target? [y/N] ")?;
217	            if !response.eq_ignore_ascii_case("y") {
218	                return Err("aborted".into());
219	            }
220	        }
221	    }
222	
223	    if plan.action == SymlinkAction::AlreadyCorrect {
224	        log::info!(
225	            "Already correct: {} -> {}",
226	            plan.symlink_path.display(),
227	            plan.abs_target.display()
228	        );
229	    } else {
230	        execute_plan(&plan, true)?;
231	        log::info!(
232	            "Created: {} -> {}",
233	            plan.symlink_path.display(),
234	            plan.abs_target.display()
235	        );
236	    }
237	
238	    if args.list {
239	        log::info!("");
240	        log::info!("Contents of {}:", abs_target.display());
241	        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&abs_target)? {
242	            let entry = entry?;
243	            log::info!("  {}", entry.file_name().to_string_lossy());
244	        }
245	    }
246	
247	    Ok(())
248	}

symlink(args: &SymlinkArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;\n\n    let target = match &args.target {\n        Some(t) => PathBuf::from(t),\n        None => PathBuf::from(\".claude\"),\n    };\n\n    let symlink_dir = match &args.symlink_dir {\n        Some(d) => d.clone(),\n        None => {\n            let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\")\n                .map_err(|_| \"HOME environment variable not set\".to_string())?;\n            PathBuf::from(home).join(\".claude\").join(\"projects\")\n        }\n    };\n\n    let sl = SymLink::new(&cwd, &target, &symlink_dir)?;\n\n    // Handle interactive prompt for replacement\n    if let SymlinkAction::Replace { ref current_target } = sl.action {\n        log::info!(\n            \"Existing symlink: {} -> {}\",\n            sl.symlink_path.display(),\n            current_target.display()\n        );\n        if !args.yes {\n            let response = crate::common::prompt(\"Replace with new target? [y/N] \")?;\n            if !response.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"y\") {\n                return Err(\"aborted\".into());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if sl.action == SymlinkAction::AlreadyCorrect {\n        log::info!(\n            \"Already correct: {} -> {}\",\n            sl.symlink_path.display(),\n            sl.abs_target.display()\n        );\n    } else {\n        sl.create(true)?;\n        log::info!(\n            \"Created: {} -> {}\",\n            sl.symlink_path.display(),\n            sl.abs_target.display()\n        );\n    }\n\n    if args.list {\n        let abs_target = if target.is_absolute() {\n            target\n        } else {\n            cwd.join(&target)\n        };\n        log::info!(\"\");\n        log::info!(\"Contents of {}:\", abs_target.display());\n        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&abs_target)? {\n            let entry = entry?;\n            log::info!(\"  {}\", entry.file_name().to_string_lossy());\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn encode_path_basic() {\n        assert_eq!(\n target, symlink_dir, None).unwrap();\n\n        assert_eq!(sl.abs_target, PathBuf::from(\"/home/user/project/.claude\"));\n        assert_eq!(\n            sl.symlink_path,\n            PathBuf::from(\"/home/user/.claude/projects/-home-user-project\")\n        );\n        assert_eq!(sl.action, SymlinkAction::Create);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn new_already_correct() {\n        let > DEVELOPER

I'm a little surprized it's 31 lines longer, but no big deal.
One question you imply symlinks are only on Unix, but ask google or .. and MacOS and Windows do support symlinks, IIRC. Although, maybe too `~/.claude/projects/` isn't used and on those systems claude-code works differently?

> AGENT

Good question. macOS is Unix — it's covered by `#[cfg(unix)]`. The `#[cfg(not(unix))]` error path is really just for Windows.

Windows does support symlinks (`std::os::windows::fs::symlink_dir`), but it requires elevated privileges or developer mode. And you're right that Claude Code might handle the projects directory differently on Windows — it may not use symlinks at all there.

For now the `#[cfg(not(unix))]` error is fine since vc-x1 is a jj+git CLI tool that's realistically Unix/macOS only. If Windows support ever matters, it's a one-line addition:

```rust
#[cfg(windows)]
std::os::windows::fs::symlink_dir(&self.abs_target, &self.symlink_path)?;
```

Not worth doing until there's a user for it. Want to commit dev2?

16	/// Parsed file limit: None (suppress), Some(n) (cap at n), or all.
17	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
18	pub enum FileLimit {
19	    /// Don't show changed files section at all.
20	    None,
21	    /// Show up to N files (with first/last split if truncated).
22	    Cap(usize),
23	    /// Show all files.
24	    All,
25	}
26	
27	impl FileLimit {
28	    fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
29	        match s {
30	            "0" => Ok(FileLimit::None),
31	            "all" => Ok(FileLimit::All),
32	            _ => s
33	                .parse::<usize>()
34	                .map(FileLimit::Cap)
35	                .map_err(|_| format!("invalid file limit '{s}': expected number, 0, or 'all'")),
36	        }
37	    }
38	}

40	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
41	pub struct ShowArgs {
42	    #[command(flatten)]
43	    pub common: common::CommonArgs,
44	
45	    /// Max changed files: number, 0 (none), or 'all'
46	    #[arg(short = 'f', long = "files", default_value = "50")]
47	    pub files: String,
48	}

50	pub fn show(args: &ShowArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
51	    let file_limit = FileLimit::parse(&args.files)?;
52	    let c = &args.common;
53	
54	    let spec = common::resolve_spec(c.pos_rev.as_deref(), c.pos_count, &c.revision, c.limit, "@");
55	    let hdr = common::resolve_header(&c.label, c.no_label);
56	
57	    common::for_each_repo(&c.repos, &hdr, |workspace, repo| {
58	        let (ids, anchor_index) =
59	            common::collect_ids(workspace, repo, &spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count)?;
60	
61	        let mut first = true;
62	        for (i, commit_id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {
63	            if !first {
64	                println!("────────────────────────────────────────");
65	            }
66	            first = false;
67	
68	            let commit = repo.store().get_commit(commit_id)?;
69	            show_one_commit(&commit, workspace, repo, file_limit, i == anchor_index)?;
70	        }
71	        Ok(())
72	    })
73	}
74	
75	fn show_one_commit(
76	    commit: &Commit,
77	    workspace: &Workspace,
78	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
79	    file_limit: FileLimit,
80	    is_primary: bool,
81	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
82	    // Author
83	    let author = commit.author();
84	    println!(
85	        "Author:    {} <{}> ({})",
86	        author.name,
87	        author.email,
88	        format_timestamp(&author.timestamp)
89	    );
90	
91	    // Committer
92	    let committer = commit.committer();
93	    println!(
94	        "Committer: {} <{}> ({})",
95	        committer.name,
96	        committer.email,
97	        format_timestamp(&committer.timestamp)
98	    );
99	
100	    // Ids
101	    let ids_line = common::format_commit_short(commit);
102	    if is_primary {
103	        println!("Ids:       {}", common::bold(&ids_line));
104	    } else {
105	        println!("Ids:       {ids_line}");
106	    }
107	
108	    // Parents
109	    let root_commit_id = repo.store().root_commit_id().clone();
110	    for parent_id in commit.parent_ids() {
111	        if *parent_id == root_commit_id {
112	            continue;
113	        }
114	        let parent = repo.store().get_commit(parent_id)?;
115	        println!("Parent:    {}", common::format_commit_short(&parent));
116	    }
117	
118	    // Children
119	    let children_ids =
120	        common::resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &format!("children({})", commit.id().hex()))?;
121	    for child_id in &children_ids {
122	        if *child_id == root_commit_id {
123	            continue;
124	        }
125	        let child = repo.store().get_commit(child_id)?;
126	        println!("Child:     {}", common::format_commit_short(&child));
127	    }
128	
129	    // Branches
130	    let branches_str = format_branches(commit, workspace, repo)?;
131	    println!("Branches:  {branches_str}");
132	
133	    // Follows
134	    let follows = find_nearest_tag(commit, workspace, repo, true)?;
135	    println!("Follows:   {}", follows.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
136	
137	    // Precedes
138	    let precedes = find_nearest_tag(commit, workspace, repo, false)?;
139	    println!("Precedes:  {}", precedes.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
140	
141	    // Description (body only — title is on the Ids line)
142	    print_description(commit);
143	
144	    // Changed files
145	    if file_limit != FileLimit::None {
146	        print_diff(commit, repo, file_limit)?;
147	    }
148	
149	    Ok(())
150	}
151	
152	fn find_nearest_tag(
153	    commit: &Commit,
154	    workspace: &Workspace,
155	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
156	    ancestor: bool,
157	) -> Result<Option<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
158	    let commit_hex = commit.id().hex();
159	
160	    let revset_str = if ancestor {
161	        format!("heads(tags() & ::{})", commit_hex)
162	    } else {
163	        format!("roots(tags() & {}::)", commit_hex)
164	    };
165	
166	    let tag_ids = common::resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &revset_str)?;
167	    if tag_ids.is_empty() {
168	        return Ok(None);
169	    }
170	
171	    let tag_id = &tag_ids[0];
172	    let view = repo.view();
173	    for (name, local_remote) in view.tags() {
174	        if local_remote.local_target.added_ids().any(|id| id == tag_id) {
175	            return Ok(Some(name.as_str().to_string()));
176	        }
177	    }
178	
179	    Ok(None)
180	}
181	
182	fn format_branches(
183	    commit: &Commit,
184	    workspace: &Workspace,
185	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
186	) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
187	    let commit_hex = commit.id().hex();
188	    let view = repo.view();
189	    let mut names: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
190	
191	    for (name, local_remote) in view.bookmarks() {
192	        for bookmark_id in local_remote.local_target.added_ids() {
193	            let revset_str = format!("{} & ::{}", commit_hex, bookmark_id.hex());
194	            let results = common::resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &revset_str)?;
195	            if !results.is_empty() {
196	                names.push(name.as_str().to_string());
197	                break;
198	            }
199	        }
200	
201	        for (remote_name, remote_ref) in &local_remote.remote_refs {
202	            if remote_name.as_str() == "git" {
203	                continue;
204	            }
205	            for bookmark_id in remote_ref.target.added_ids() {
206	                let revset_str = format!("{} & ::{}", commit_hex, bookmark_id.hex());
207	                let results = common::resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &revset_str)?;
208	                if !results.is_empty() {
209	                    names.push(format!("{}@{}", name.as_str(), remote_name.as_str()));
210	                    break;
211	                }
212	            }
213	        }
214	    }
215	
216	    Ok(names.join(", "))
217	}

219	fn format_timestamp(ts: &jj_lib::backend::Timestamp) -> String {
220	    let millis = ts.timestamp.0;
221	    let secs = millis / 1000;
222	    let tz_minutes = ts.tz_offset;
223	
224	    let dt = chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp(secs, 0)
225	        .unwrap_or_default()
226	        .with_timezone(
227	            &chrono::FixedOffset::east_opt(tz_minutes * 60).unwrap_or(chrono::Utc.fix()),
228	        );
229	
230	    dt.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S").to_string()
231	}
232	
233	fn print_description(commit: &Commit) {
234	    let desc = commit.description();
235	    let body: String = desc
236	        .lines()
237	        .skip(1)
238	        .skip_while(|l| l.is_empty())
239	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
240	        .join("\n");
241	
242	    println!("Description:");
243	    for line in body.lines() {
244	        println!("    {line}");
245	    }
246	}
247	
248	fn print_diff(
249	    commit: &Commit,
250	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
251	    file_limit: FileLimit,
252	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
253	    let parent_tree = commit.parent_tree(repo.as_ref()).block_on()?;
254	    let commit_tree = commit.tree();
255	
256	    let diff_iter = TreeDiffIterator::new(&parent_tree, &commit_tree, &EverythingMatcher);
257	
258	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
259	    for entry in diff_iter {
260	        let diff = entry.values?;
261	        let before = diff.before.as_resolved().cloned().flatten();
262	        let after = diff.after.as_resolved().cloned().flatten();
263	
264	        if matches!(&before, Some(TreeValue::Tree(_))) || matches!(&after, Some(TreeValue::Tree(_)))
265	        {
266	            continue;
267	        }
268	
269	        let path_str = entry.path.as_internal_file_string().to_string();
270	
271	        let line = match (before, after) {
272	            (None, Some(value)) => {
273	                format!("    Added {} {path_str}", file_type_str(&value))
274	            }
275	            (Some(_), None) => {
276	                format!(
277	                    "    Removed {} {path_str}",
278	                    file_type_str_from_merged(&diff.before),
279	                )
280	            }
281	            (Some(_), Some(value)) => {
282	                format!("    Modified {} {path_str}", file_type_str(&value))
283	            }
284	            (None, None) => continue,
285	        };
286	        lines.push(line);
287	    }
288	
289	    let total = lines.len();
290	    let cap = match file_limit {
291	        FileLimit::All | FileLimit::None => 0,
292	        FileLimit::Cap(n) => n,
293	    };
294	    let show_all = cap == 0 || total <= cap;
295	
296	    if show_all {
297	        println!("Changed files: {total}");
298	        for line in &lines {
299	            println!("{line}");
300	        }
301	    } else {
302	        println!("Changed files: {total}, showing first {cap}");
303	        for line in &lines[..cap] {
304	            println!("{line}");
305	        }
306	    }
307	
308	    Ok(())
309	}
310	
311	fn file_type_str(value: &TreeValue) -> &'static str {
312	    match value {
313	        TreeValue::File {
314	            executable: false, ..
315	        } => "regular file",
316	        TreeValue::File {
317	            executable: true, ..
318	        } => "executable file",
319	        TreeValue::Symlink(_) => "symlink",
320	        TreeValue::Tree(_) => "tree",
321	        TreeValue::GitSubmodule(_) => "git submodule",
322	    }
323	}
324	
325	fn file_type_str_from_merged(merged: &jj_lib::merge::Merge<Option<TreeValue>>) -> &'static str {
326	    if let Some(Some(value)) = merged.as_resolved() {
327	        file_type_str(value)
328	    } else {
329	        "file"
330	    }
331	}

> DEVELOPER

Since we're almost done, why the convention log::info! ... and not just info! or debug! ...

> AGENT

In init.rs I imported them at the top: `use log::{debug, info};` — so it uses bare `info!`, `debug!`. In the other files I used the fully qualified `log::info!` to avoid adding an import for just one or two calls.

Either way works — it's inconsistent though. Want me to pick one convention? I'd suggest bare `info!`/`debug!` with imports everywhere, since it's shorter and matches init.rs.

> DEVELOPER

Which is more common in rust, log:: prefix or not?

> AGENT

Both are common. The `log` crate docs show bare `info!`, `debug!` etc. — that's the intended API. The `log::` prefix is more common when there's only one call in a file and you don't want to add an import line.

For a codebase like ours where most files use it, bare macros with `use log::{info, debug, ...}` at the top is cleaner and more idiomatic. Let's standardize on that?
